paragraphs.text: # dsh-skill-pdf-math

A DeepSeek Harness skill for reading
mathematics out of PDFs and formula screenshots **without guess

Seek Harness skill for reading
mathematics out of PDFs and formula screenshots **without guessing**.
## Why

Vision models misread formulas in predictable ways: a `\mathcal{L}` becomes `\angle`,
a summation su

bscript `j=1` becomes `\cdot`, a tall bracket turns into `[[[`.
Most of that is unnecessary, because

a LaTeX-produced PDF stores formulas as
**positioned text**, not images — glyphs, baselines, sizes
and font names are all there.
So the skill teaches one rule:
> read the text layer first, let formula OCR supply the structure, and cross-check the two.
## What it adds

- `pdf_formula.py` — turns a PDF region into readable (approximate) LaTeX by restoring
sub/superscri

pts from baseline offsets, plus a small TeX `cmex10` operator table.
- `--probe` — decides whether a

page's formulas are extractable text or images.
- `--crosscheck` — compares the OCR result against

the text layer's letters **and their fonts**
(`cmsy10`'s `L` *is* `\mathcal{L}`), so a wrong glyph i

s named instead of merely suspected.
- `--verify` — re-recognises with a different crop and resoluti
on; disagreement is reported.
Measured on four numbered equations from a real paper:
| render | mean similarity | exact |

`--check` requires the optional `rapid_latex_ocr` runtime; without it the text-layer
channel still w
orks and the skill says so instead of failing.
